issues.description: Attribute de.tum.in.ase.eist.model.Person.id has conflicting types across artifacts: the problem statement describes REST endpoints using UUID path variables (/persons/{personId}) and the template model (src/common/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/model/Person.java) declares the id field as java.util.UUID (private UUID id;). In the solution repository the same model (src/common/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/model/Person.java) declares id as Long (private Long id;). This cross-artifact attribute type mismatch (UUID vs Long) will confuse students about the intended ID type and can lead to compilation errors or incorrect implementations when wiring the REST layer, service layer and client.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Person.id type consistent across all artifacts. Preferred resolution: change the solution's Person.id back to java.util.UUID to match the problem statement and template, and update any solution code that assumes Long (adjust imports and places where id is compared/created). Alternative: if Long IDs are intended, update the problem statement, template model, and all REST signatures and client code to use Long consistently. Do not mix UUID and Long types across model, service, resource, and client.

issues.description: Solution repository internal inconsistency: in src/server/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/rest/PersonResource.java the REST method signatures use java.util.UUID for the personId path variable (e.g., updatePerson(@RequestBody Person updatedPerson, @PathVariable("personId") UUID personId)), while the solution's model (src/common/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/model/Person.java) declares id as Long. This mismatch between the REST resource parameter types and the model field type will cause type inconsistencies and likely compilation errors in the solution code base.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the ID type within the solution repository. Either: (A) change the PersonResource @PathVariable and method parameter types from UUID to Long (and remove/replace java.util.UUID imports), and ensure PersonService and client use Long; or (B, preferred given the template/problem) change the solution's Person.id back to java.util.UUID and update PersonService, client PersonController and any comparisons/assignments accordingly so that model, service, REST resource, and client consistently use UUID.

issues.description: Concept: the primary identifier field of the Person model (Person.id). Problem statement and the template common model declare Person.id as a UUID (problem statement UML: Person.id: UUID; template: src/common/.../Person.java declares private UUID id;). In the solution repository the common Person model declares Person.id as a Long (solution src/common/.../Person.java: private Long id;), but the solution server-side artifacts (PersonResource method signatures and PersonService) still use UUID in path variable types and when generating new IDs (e.g. UUID personId path variable in PersonResource.updatePerson and person.setId(UUID.randomUUID()) in PersonService). This produces a cross-artifact type mismatch for the same conceptual identifier (UUID vs Long) that prevents a clear mapping from the problem requirements and template to the solution implementation, will confuse students about which ID type to use in client/server requests, and can lead to compile/runtime errors.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Person.id type consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fix: revert the solution common model to use UUID for Person.id to match the problem statement and template. Concretely, change solution_repository/src/common/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/model/Person.java to declare private UUID id; and update its getter/setter signatures accordingly. Ensure solution server code (PersonResource path variable types and PersonService ID generation) also use UUID consistently. Alternatively (less preferred) unify everything to Long by changing the problem statement, template Person.java, and all server/client handling to use Long and adjust ID-generation accordingly. Ensure all method signatures, path variables, and JSON (de)serialization consistently use the chosen type.
